nodes.label: Elevated γ-glutamyl transpeptidase (γ-GT) level and hyperferritinemia present for many years
A 40-year-old man was referred to the medical center for these laboratory abnormalities and reported no liver-related symptoms
The patient had no history of alcohol misuse or use of hepatotoxic drugs; his parents and siblings were all phenotypically normal
Physical examination revealed hepatomegaly (18.9 cm), splenomegaly (13.2 cm × 4.2 cm), and body mass index of 26 kg/m²
Serum ferritin is elevated at 621 µg/L
GPT gene variants are of uncertain significance
Metabolic syndrome features: low adiponectin, high HOMA-IR, hypertriglyceridemia, low HDL, and hepatic steatosis
Liver stiffness measurement is 6.7 kPa (no significant fibrosis)
Non-HFE hereditary iron overload (e.g., ferroportin disease)
Metabolic fatty liver disease without iron overload
Metabolic fatty liver disease with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH)
HFE mutation analysis has not been performed
Hepatic MRI T2* iron quantification has not been performed
Non-HFE gene panel has not been performed
Liver biopsy iron quantification has not been performed
